units: RAHU package describes synthetic contradiction environments, telemetry, and benchmark execution interfaces.
Package imports and exports only the evaluator module.
RAHUResult stores task ID, LBR, confidence pre/post, structural distance, update indicator, ARR, latency, ADI, and ACS.
Harness uses structural distance threshold 0.35 by default.
evaluate gets phase-1 observations and calls agent.commit_mechanism.
evaluate calls environment.apply_adversarial_shift on the committed mechanism and reads prediction_error and LBR.
evaluate gets contradiction feedback and calls agent.receive_feedback_and_update.
structural update is binary 1 when computed distance exceeds threshold, otherwise 0.
Placeholder structural distance is 0 for equality and 1 for any non-equal mechanism.
ARR helper asks agent for baseline and current invalid-mechanism authority, divides and clamps to [0,1].
Latency uses agent.get_response_latency_steps if present, else infinity.
ADI helper multiplies LBR, post-confidence, and one minus update indicator then clamps to [0,1].
ACS helper combines one minus ADI, one minus ARR, and a latency term; infinite latency yields zero.
evaluate returns RAHUResult assembled from these computed values.
Any non-equal mechanism receives distance 1.0, so the implementation does not realize the documented syntax/execution/causal structural distance.
The method requires get_baseline_authority_weight on the supplied agent but this requirement is not declared in the abstract agent interface on the frozen surface.
The evaluator does not directly invoke the frozen PTVS, MRAT, AdaptiveInheritanceEngine, or REE classes despite the documented five-layer pipeline.
Computes inadmissible/total with zero returned for nonpositive total.
Computes post/pre authority, returns zero for nonpositive pre, and clamps ratio to [0,1].
Returns first index at or below threshold fraction of initial authority or None.
Builds metric dictionary from AgentTelemetry plus supplied LBR, update rate, and prediction error.
Standalone metric functions have boundary behaviors and validation semantics that differ in places from evaluator methods; no canonical implementation is designated.
No bounds or validity checks guarantee inputs keep composite metrics within their documented ranges.
